text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New tax system to be announced in the budget on January 13, Prime Minister Alfred Sant announces during annual luncheon of the Malta Chamber of Commerce.

- Parliament appoints six committees to oversee House business, MPs' privileges, public accounts, foreign affairs, social affairs and enaction of laws. Sandro Schembri Adami of the ruling Labour Party heads the Foreign Affairs Committee. Former finance minister John Dalli of the opposition Nationalists is chairman of the Public Accounts Committee.
- Local elections to be held in March.
- Prisoners to be given chance to rehabilitate themselves outside the prisons.
- Government committed to help private enterprise remain competitive, prime minister tells Chamber of Commerce.

- Government terminates contract of state broadcasting head Tony Mallia, recently praised in a government report for taking company into profit after heavy losses last year. He was criticised however for his relations with the employees, and a government-appointed expert recommended termination of his contract so the station could start a new era.
